Pixel Blade · the mark · round eight

The
Vessel

E1's rock, E1's lip, the Monk on stone rather than on the moon — carrying E2's tree. Solid white, shadow kept, Monk up a quarter.

01 · The lead

F2

The merge landed. The rock is a real outcrop now and the Monk sits on the stone, not on the rim — which was the note that mattered most, because a figure perched on the object reads as decoration and a figure sitting on ground inside it reads as inhabitant.

Deep bowl at the bottom lip. E2's canopy in wide layered tiers, reaching left past the crescent's own silhouette. The pale scoop band runs broad along the inner face. Monk at roughly a tenth of frame height.

02 · Night

FN1

The scoop turns bronze again, and on the deeper bowl it reads better than any night plate so far — a long warm blade of light down the inner face with the rock and the Monk sitting in front of it.

Worth noticing: this is the second round where a night prompt closed the crescent into a full ring on its own (EN1, now FN2). Twice is a pattern, not an accident. A closed annulus holds a dark interior better than an open mouth, because the mouth has nothing to bleed into but the ground. If night ever fights us, that is the reason and the ring is the fix.

FN1 · night lead · 89.0% dark

03 · The rest of the round

Alternates

04 · The white

It was never
pure white

I flagged a conflict before generating: tokens.css rejects pure white for the day ground — "not pure white (clinical), not cream (nostalgic)" — and #FFFFFF misses the edge tolerance against #F4F5F2 by a single point.

It did not bite. Asked for solid white, the render returned 241–249 across the corners, within 7 of paper. Every day plate passes the edge check untouched. The instruction and the token were never actually in conflict — what reads as "solid white" to the eye is already paper.

A paper-locked copy of the lead exists anyway (vessel-f2paper.jpg, edge delta 0) if you ever want the mark to sit on the exact day ground rather than near it.

06 · Settled

The kasa is
written down

Ruled in and recorded in monk.md, so it stops being a contradiction the next session quietly removes.

The rule as written: the kasa is permitted when the Monk appears inside a mark or a made object at roughly a tenth of frame height or smaller, and forbidden in environment plates and portraits, where the layered wardrobe does the work and a hat would flatten him toward the student. It is a legibility exception. Nothing in the mythos follows from it, the Samurai's hat still means what it meant, and a kasa found in a full-size plate is a bug.

07 · Small

Handed to
the kamon

The bigger Monk buys a little more legibility on the way down — he now survives to about 96px rather than 128. Below that the kamon takes over.

08 · Open

Two decisions

Is F2 the mark

It answers every note in the brief. If it is, the next move is not another variant — it is locking one plate and building the kamon beside it, so the system has both halves.

The ring keeps coming back

Three times now across two rounds the annulus has appeared unasked — as EN1, as FN2, and as the Rim Window in the first concept set. It may be the night form of the same object rather than a rival to it. Worth one deliberate test rather than continuing to arrive at it by accident.
